key_insight: EVATok adaptively allocates token budget across a video's temporal blocks so simple/repetitive segments use fewer tokens while complex/dynamic segments get more, preserving reconstruction quality with fewer overall tokens.
problem_solved: Uniform-length video tokenization wastes tokens on easy frames and under-represents complex ones, forcing a tradeoff between reconstruction fidelity and autoregressive generation cost; EVATok resolves this inefficiency by variable-rate token assignment.
method: Compute per-block complexity/motion cues and use them to decide token allocation rather than a fixed token count per block.
Use a variable-rate tokenizer (learned or rule-based allocator) to produce shorter discrete token sequences for simple segments and denser codes for complex segments.
Integrate the adaptive token stream with an autoregressive video generator to maintain generation quality while reducing sequence length and compute.
impact: Reduces token sequence length and autoregressive compute without sacrificing visual fidelity, enabling faster, more cost-effective video generation pipelines and scaling AR models to longer or higher-resolution videos.

paper_title: EVATok: Adaptive Length Video Tokenization for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Tianwei Xiong, Jun Hao Liew, Zilong Huang, Zhijie Lin, Jiashi Feng
